meanings.note: слава богу = thank God (literally 'glory to God')

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?
He is running in the election.

examples.text: У меня много дел. Выборы мэра…
examples.trans: I've got a lot to do. The mayoral election...

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: collective number for people and children, + genitive plural: двое детей

examples.trans: Well, yes. A wife, two kids.

examples.text: А у меня все шансы есть. Жена, двое детей, не сидел, служил в армии.
examples.trans: And I've got every chance. A wife, two kids, no prison record, I served in the army.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.en: to guess, to work out, to think of

examples.trans: Why didn't I think of it at once!

examples.text: Какой глупый человек догадался это сделать?
examples.trans: What foolish person thought of doing that?

examples.text: Ты никогда сам не догадаешься об этом.
examples.trans: You will never guess this by yourself.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.

meanings.note: Как вы знаете = as you know.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Уже месяц = for a month now.

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Head of a town. Borrowed from French 'maire' (from Latin 'maior', greater/senior official).

examples.trans: He is the mayor of the town.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Вот оно! Самсон, ты будешь новым мэром.
examples.trans: That's it! Samson, you'll be the new mayor.

examples.text: Ага! Вот оно в чём дело.
examples.trans: Aha! So that's what it's about.

examples.text: Спа захотела? Вот оно, твоё королевство!
examples.trans: Wanted a spa? There it is, your kingdom!

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?
Russian. Orthodox. Never been in prison.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Also a Russian man (as a noun).

examples.trans: Russian. Orthodox. Never been in prison.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.
Why are you sitting in the corner?

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

examples.text: Слава богу! Я пьяных за рулём просто терпеть не могу!
examples.trans: Thank goodness! I simply cannot stand drunk people behind the wheel!

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: На стройке = at a building site.

examples.trans: I work on a building site.
The building site is next to the house.
Everything's fine. I work on a building site.

examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: + accusative: через неделю = in a week

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

examples.text: Наш новый сосед эфиоп, он отлично варит кофе.
examples.trans: Our new neighbour is Ethiopian, he makes excellent coffee.
